about.title: Clayton Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Clayton is a small place. With fewer than 12,000 residents, a death here is rarely anonymous — neighbors along Oakhurst Drive and Keller Ridge Drive usually know who was lost. Public records show the city closed 2025 with 8 injury collisions, 9 people hurt, and no traffic deaths. When a Clayton family does face a sudden loss — a collision on Clayton Road or Marsh Creek Road, a fall, a defective product, or medical care that went wrong — few people nearby have walked that road before. California's wrongful death law gives certain family members the right to bring a civil claim in their own name. Standing goes first to a spouse or registered domestic partner and children, then to specific dependents and heirs. The claim is separate from any criminal case and generally must be filed within two years of the date of death, sooner if a public agency is involved. LawProactive is not a law firm. We connect Clayton families, at no cost, with an independent attorney who works on contingency.

whyChoose.title: What a Clayton Family Should Know Before Filing

items.title: Not everyone can bring the claim
items.desc: California limits who may file: a surviving spouse or registered domestic partner and children come first, followed by certain dependents and heirs. An attorney can confirm where you and your relatives stand before anything is filed.

items.title: The clock runs from the date of death
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims in California must be filed within two years of the date of death. If a city, county or state agency may share responsibility, that window is considerably shorter, so early contact matters.

items.title: A civil claim, separate from any criminal case
items.desc: A wrongful death action does not depend on whether prosecutors file charges or win a conviction. It seeks recovery for funeral and burial costs, lost financial support, and the loss of love, companionship and guidance.

items.question: Clayton recorded no traffic deaths in 2025. Do wrongful death claims still happen here?
items.answer: Yes. Traffic collisions are only one source of these claims, and Clayton families have also lost loved ones to falls, unsafe products, medical errors and incidents on the job. A Clayton resident may also be killed in a crash outside city limits, elsewhere in Contra Costa County or beyond, and the claim can still be handled locally. An attorney will look at the specific facts rather than the citywide numbers.

items.question: There is a criminal case against the person responsible. Do we have to wait for it to end?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action that runs on its own track, and the two-year filing deadline does not pause while a criminal case unfolds. Waiting for a verdict could put the civil claim at risk. Many families pursue both at the same time, and an attorney can coordinate around the criminal proceedings.

items.question: How does LawProactive fit in, and what does it cost?
items.answer: LawProactive is not a law firm and does not represent you. We are a free service that connects Clayton families with an independent personal injury attorney who handles wrongful death cases. Attorneys in the network work on contingency, meaning there is no fee unless there is a recovery, and there is no charge for the connection itself.
